name: gizza-ai/csv-sample
summary: Sample rows from a CSV (random, systematic, top/bottom-N, or stratified)

tool.description: Take a sample of a CSV's data rows. `method` is random (uniform), systematic (every k-th after a seeded start), top (first N), bottom (last N), or stratified (proportional across the distinct values of `stratify_column`). Size is `n` rows, or a `percent` (0–100) of the rows when percent > 0. Random draws are reproducible via `seed`. The header row is preserved and the input delimiter is used for the output.

data.description: The CSV text to sample rows from.

delimiter.description: Field delimiter of the input, also used for the output. Default comma.

header.description: Treat the first row as a header (always kept, and used to resolve stratify_column names). Default true.

method.description: Sampling method: random (uniform), systematic (every k-th after a seeded start), top (first N), bottom (last N), or stratified (proportional across the values of stratify_column). Default random.

n.description: Number of data rows to sample. Ignored when percent > 0. Capped at the row count. Default 10.

percent.description: Sample this percentage (0–100) of data rows instead of n; 0 means use n. Default 0.

seed.description: Seed for the reproducible PRNG used by random/systematic/stratified sampling. Change it for a different draw. Default 42.

stratify_column.description: For method=stratified: the column to stratify on — a header name (header=true) or a 1-based index. Each distinct value forms a stratum sampled in proportion to its size.
